prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has concussion. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1424; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just say I'm the driver of the blue sedan involved in the accident. You can use the claim number.

Q: Understood. Can you describe what happened when the vehicles collided?
A: I was heading down the main road in Pasadena, Texas, going maybe twenty miles an hour because traffic was slow. The other car drifted into my lane and we ended up nose to nose. It didn't feel like a big impact, more like a hard jolt.

Q: Did the airbags deploy in your vehicle?
A: No, they didn't. My head snapped forward and then back against the seat, and I hit the steering wheel with my chest.

Q: Did you lose consciousness at any point?
A: I don't think so, but everything went fuzzy for a few seconds. I remember the other driver talking to me, but I couldn't answer right away.

Q: How are you feeling now?
A: Honestly, not great. I have a constant headache, I'm sensitive to light, and I get dizzy if I look at screens too long. My doctor said it looks like a concussion.

Q: Have you been seen by a medical provider since the collision?
A: Yes, I was evaluated at an urgent care clinic the same day and then I followed up with my primary physician. I've been told to limit reading and stay away from loud places for a while.

Q: Have you missed time from work?
A: Yes, I've been out since the accident because I can't focus through a full workday. I'm waiting on my doctor to say when I can go back, possibly in stages.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: Only that I want my symptoms documented accurately. Some days are better than others, and I'd like the adjuster to note that.
